info.title: Permguard decision evidence
info.description: The decision log on the control plane: shipping signed batches, reading blocks of records, and the signer manifest.

200.description: The batch is stored, or was already held.

400.description: Not a decision batch, or unattributable or unverifiable.

409.description: Out of order (`OutOfOrder`), or the stream forked or is closed (WireError).

503.description: The store or the producer keys are unavailable; the shipper retries.

DecisionBody.description: A decision record: one answer, and what it was answered from (`kind` is `decision`). Open: a reader digests and keeps a member it does not know, so a newer producer may add members.

prev.description: The digest of `seq - 1`, or the genesis.

id.description: Joins this record to the response the caller received.

causes.description: Present exactly when `outcome` is `indeterminate`: sorted, distinct `evaluation_*` codes.

context.description: The context members the deployment named in `include`.

prev.description: The digest of `seq - 1`, or the genesis.

Record.description: A decision-log record, switched on `kind`. Digested and stored verbatim.
Record.x-grpc-note: Part of the decision record, which gRPC carries as JSON bytes (never re-encoded as protobuf, so the digests hold): an element of `records` in permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse and of the batch in permguard.control.v1.ShipRequest.batch.

Envelope.description: What a batch attests to. Not a JSON member of the request: it is the canonical JSON inside `signature.payload` (base64url).

first_seq.description: The first sequence in the batch.

last_seq.description: The last sequence in the batch.

count.description: How many records it carries: `last_seq - first_seq + 1`.

previous_head.description: The head of the previous batch, or the genesis.

head.description: The digest of the record at `last_seq`.

merkle_root.description: The Merkle root over the digests of the records.

Envelope.x-grpc-note: The signed envelope payload, carried as JSON bytes inside the `batch` field of permguard.control.v1.ShipRequest (`{signature, records}`) and in an element of `proof` of permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse; never a protobuf message.

Protected.description: The protected header of a batch signature. Not a JSON member of the request: it is the JSON inside `signature.protected` (base64url).

kid.description: Which key, in the producer's published set.

Protected.x-grpc-note: The protected header of the signature, carried as JSON bytes within `batch` of permguard.control.v1.ShipRequest and within `proof` of permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse.

Signed.description: A JWS in its flattened JSON serialisation.

payload.description: The payload, base64url: the canonical envelope bytes.

Signed.x-grpc-note: The signed envelope, carried as JSON bytes: the `signature` member of the batch in `batch` of permguard.control.v1.ShipRequest, and an element of `proof` of permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse.

Batch.description: A batch: the signed envelope and the records verbatim.

records.description: The records, exactly as the producer wrote them.

Batch.x-grpc-note: The whole batch `{signature, records}` is the JSON content of the single `batch` bytes field of permguard.control.v1.ShipRequest; there is no per-member field (unlike the events ShipRequest-equivalent, IngestBatchRequest).

Acknowledgement.description: What a producer is told about its batch (200).

acked.description: The highest contiguous durable sequence. The producer truncates by this.

stored.description: How many records this call added.

Acknowledgement.x-grpc-note: The 200 answer. gRPC answers a replay or a run-ahead with the same message and an OK status; the out-of-order members have no member here because REST answers them with a 409 (OutOfOrder).

OutOfOrder.description: What a producer that ran ahead is told (409). Not the shared refusal envelope: it has `status`, not `class`/`code`.

status.x-grpc-note: REST: the string constant `out_of_order`; gRPC: the boolean `out_of_order` set true.

OutOfOrder.x-grpc-note: The REST 409 body. gRPC answers the run-ahead with an OK status and ShipResponse{out_of_order: true, expected_seq}; `acked` and `stored` exist only on that gRPC answer (the REST 409 carries neither).

DecisionBlock.description: One page of decision records: the common stream block with typed records.

next.description: Opaque authenticated offset for the following block.

high_watermark.description: The exclusive end this read observed, echoed as `until`.

proof.description: The signed envelopes covering these records, when `proof` was asked.

inclusion.description: One inclusion path per record, when `proof` was asked.

DecisionBlock.x-grpc-note: `records`, `proof` and `inclusion` are JSON objects here and elements of `repeated bytes` (each the JSON text) on gRPC.

StreamSignersView.description: One producer stream's signer history with the receiver's durable frontier.

acked.description: Everything through this sequence is durable here.
